symbols.note: from gatekit symbols system --dll dx11 --full; no per-method address was found in bg3_dx11.exe for these methods (null); factory/constructor/update come from survey.csv, which prints them as bg3.exe+RVA, the same offsets the dx11 symbols users list shows
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Called by outside code (the entity-conversion helpers for items and characters call it, found by a text search of the pseudo-code) to queue an (entity, yes/no) request; it only stores the request in two parallel lists on the system.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x367420 read; callers listed by gatekit decomp grep: esv::EntityConversionHelpers::AddItem and AddCharacter.

does.text: For each queued entity that is still alive: if the request says no and the entity has eoc::improvised_weapon::CanBeWieldedComponent, the component is removed; if the request says yes and the entity lacks it, a helper adds it. The type was resolved from the helper functions' type-index global.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x366E50 read: alive check, has-component helper EoCServer.dll+0x3666C0 and add helper EoCServer.dll+0x366480 both resolve to CanBeWieldedComponent, RemoveComponentUnchecked uses the same type index. The yes branch (add) was inferred from the helper, the guard read is 'not has component'.

unknown: Which conversion rule decides yes or no at AddItem and AddCharacter was not read, so what exactly makes an item an improvised weapon is unknown.
Update's own body was not read; that it calls ProcessChanges is a guess from the method list.
sure: no: the guard and the add/remove were read, but the source of the yes/no value was not
